messages:
alex.s: Customer ACME reports intermittent 502/504s to their private deployment behind Azure WAF since cert rotation at 06:00 UTC. Latency spikes to 5-8s then timeouts. Not consistently reproducible.
customer:acme-corp: seeing 'upstream reset' in our gateway logs and half of our requests fail during peak, started right after we rotated certs and uploaded new bundle.
maria.c: can you share the HAProxy / nginx front proxy logs? also, did they upload a custom chain or are we managing the certs?
customer:acme-corp: we uploaded our own bundle (PEM) to the private console. Azure WAF sits in front, it terminates TLS and proxies to the VPC VIP. We also use Azure App Gateway with a NAT GW.
jamal.o: quick hypothesis: Azure WAF or NAT is blocking egress to OCSP responders -> OCSP timeout -> handshake stalls -> long tail latency and upstream resets. But also if uploaded bundle misses intermediate or has wrong order, some clients re-request and create retry storms.
ingrid.oncall: can we get a repro? ask customer to run these from their gateway host and paste output:

openssl s_client -connect vip.private.internal:443 -servername api.acme.example.com -status -showcerts
# and a curl with verbose TLS handshake
curl -v --max-time 10 https://api.acme.example.com/healthz 2>&1 | sed -n '1,200p'

customer:acme-corp: attached outputs below (redacted IPs).

customer:acme-corp: ```
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=2 C = US, O = ExampleRoot, CN = Example Root CA
verify return:1
depth=1 C = US, O = Acme Intermediate, CN = Acme Intermediate CA
verify return:1
depth=0 CN = api.acme.example.com
verify return:1
OCSP response: no response sent
---
```

alex.s: "OCSP response: no response sent" strongly suggests the server couldn't reach the OCSP responder during handshake. That would cause some clients to stall or fail depending on their TLS stack and OCSP stapling config.
maria.c: also noticed in the PEM they uploaded the chain is reversed: they put leaf -> root, but HAProxy expects leaf -> intermediate -> root. If the gateway or WAF reorders/truncates that, some downstream clients may not be able to build the chain without fetching the intermediate. Combined with OCSP egress blocked, that fits the symptoms.
jamal.o: what's our current evidence for egress blocking? any firewall/NAT rules changed around rotation time?
customer:acme-corp: we did an internal change to NSG outbound rules to tighten ephemeral ports at 05:45 UTC. That could explain it.
ingrid.oncall: ok repro plan and remediation steps:
1) Temporarily allow outbound TCP 80/443 to known OCSP endpoints and CRL distribution points for the cert issuer. (example: ocsp.acme-ca.example)
2) Re-upload corrected PEM with intermediate ordered directly after leaf: 
   -----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----
   (leaf)
   -----END CERTIFICATE-----
   -----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----
   (intermediate)
   -----END CERTIFICATE-----
   -----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----
   (root)
   -----END CERTIFICATE-----
3) On Azure WAF/App Gateway disable rewrite that strips TLS chain or ensure passthrough to backend 'preserve client cert chain' setting.
4) Retry a curl test from the gateway host and from client side.
5) Monitor latency and 5xx rates for 1 hour, roll back NSG changes if not improved.

customer:acme-corp: we opened a temporary outbound allowlist for ocsp and re-uploaded bundle in the correct order. Reproduced the openssl s_client above and now see:

customer:acme-corp: ```
OCSP Response Status: successful (0x0)
stapled response: yes
verify return:1
```

alex.s: great. results? metrics?
customer:acme-corp: 5xxs dropped from ~8% to <0.5% within 10 mins. P95 latency back to normal. No additional billing spikes observed, the earlier retry storms were transient.
maria.c: action items for us:
- add a support KB entry for 'Private deployment: common causes of OCSP timeouts during cert rotation' with commands and common responders per CA.
- console validation: warn if uploaded PEM is missing intermediate or if order doesn't match leaf->intermediate->root.
- add telemetry to detect "OCSP response: no response sent" on healthz TLS checks so we can proactively alert.

jamal.o: I'll file infra ticket to surface NSG changes correlated with cert updates so we can alert when outbound egress to known responder hosts is blocked.
ingrid.oncall: put this as Sev3 while we close loop with customer; include timeline and postmortem notes.
ops-bot: incident created: INC-2026-4309; priority: P3; assigned: eng-infra, support.
customer:acme-corp: thanks all, we'll keep the allowlist in place while we validate with our security team. Appreciate the quick help :thumbsup:
alex.s: marking resolved pending 24h observation. If any regression, escalate to oncall and we'll open a dedicated bridge.
